Ocean silicate: learning from oxygen classes and partial measurements

  • 1. Select the computation
  • 2. Explore the observed data
  • 3. Fit and make held-out predictions
  • 4. Inspect predictions and uncertainty
  • 5. Reproduce and cite

Can oxygen categories and a small number of exact oxygen measurements help predict silicate? This notebook follows that question from exploratory plots to held-out predictions using the frozen GLODAPv2.2023 North Pacific subset. The 200 observations represent distinct station profiles at 300–1,500 dbar, with oxygen below 180 µmol kg⁻¹. The response is silicate; fully observed inputs are salinity and log pressure. Oxygen is treated as partially observed, with classes bounded at 50, 100, and 150 µmol kg⁻¹.

1. Select the computation

Profile Folds Exact training oxygen Chains × iterations (warmup)
quick (this HTML example) first fold 0%, 50% 1 × 80 (30)
paper all five 0%, 20%, 50% 4 × 20,000 (5,000)

The paper workflow also runs UC-GP, LVGP, and EzGP and includes the recorded 20,000-iteration continuation step for the selected fits (fold 1/O0, fold 3/O20, fold 4/O0). Selection was based on training-chain diagnostics. The quick example demonstrates EIV-GP prediction and latent-input uncertainty; its short chain cannot establish convergence or comparative performance.

The frozen public subset and train/test files are included in data/ocean_silicate/. No separate preprocessing notebook is needed. action: "run" generates the analysis below; report rereads saved results; plan only displays settings. Supporting scripts are in codes/applications/ocean_silicate/.

profile action folds chains initial_iterations
quick run 1 1 80

2. Explore the observed data

All source oxygen measurements are retained for checking imputation; exact values are withheld according to the fixed calibration masks during fitting. Each fold has 160 training and 40 test observations. Calibration masks are nested, and no station profile appears in both training and test data in the same fold.

cohort <- ocean_read_inputs(data_dir)
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(cohort$oxygen_class)),
  col.names = c("Oxygen class (µmol/kg)", "Observations"))
Oxygen class (µmol/kg) Observations
<50 50
50–100 50
100–150 50
150–180 50 
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
p1 <- ggplot(cohort, aes(U, Y, color = oxygen_class)) + geom_point(alpha = .65) +
  labs(x = "Measured oxygen (µmol/kg)", y = "Silicate (µmol/kg)", color = "Oxygen class") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")
p2 <- ggplot(cohort, aes(oxygen_class, Y, fill = oxygen_class)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = .4) +
  labs(x = "Oxygen class (µmol/kg)", y = "Silicate (µmol/kg)") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")
p3 <- ggplot(cohort, aes(G2salinity, Y, color = log_pressure)) + geom_point(alpha = .65) +
  labs(x = "Salinity", y = "Silicate (µmol/kg)", color = "Log pressure") + theme_minimal()
p1 + p2 + p3

These plots describe the frozen subset. They do not select calibration levels, folds, or model settings based on held-out performance.

3. Fit and make held-out predictions

The class-only prediction task uses salinity, log pressure, and oxygen class. A second, mixed-information task additionally reveals the prespecified fraction of exact test oxygen values to EIV-GP. These tasks must be distinguished when interpreting scores. At zero calibration, latent oxygen is identified on the model scale; it is not scored as raw-concentration recovery.

run <- notebook_logged(paste0(output_dir, "-execution.log"),
  ocean_run_analysis(repository_dir, data_dir, output_dir, profile))

4. Inspect predictions and uncertainty

cell method RMSE MAE CRPS Coverage95
O0 EIV-GP mixed 11.083 7.634 5.839 0.825
O50 EIV-GP mixed 9.240 6.378 5.007 0.925
O0 EIV-GP xc 11.083 7.634 5.839 0.825
O50 EIV-GP xc 11.259 8.375 5.983 0.900 
ggplot(result$predictions, aes(observed_Y, predicted_Y)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(alpha = .65, color = "#2c7fb8") + facet_wrap(~cell) +
  labs(x = "Observed held-out silicate", y = "Predicted silicate",
       title = "Class-only held-out predictions") + theme_minimal()

Worked example only. One short chain cannot establish convergence; these scores are not paper results.

5. Reproduce and cite

Choose profile: "paper" and rerun this notebook to execute the complete five-fold workflow. Saved compatible fits are reused; changed inputs/settings require a separate output directory. Full diagnostic and execution logs stay in the local result directory, keeping this HTML focused on the analysis.

Data: GLODAPv2.2023 merged and adjusted product, DOI 10.25921/zyrq-ht66. Product reference: Lauvset et al. (2024), Earth System Science Data 16, 2047–2072, DOI 10.5194/essd-16-2047-2024. See the bundled data README for subset provenance and fair-data-use attribution.
